content.text: I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all four figure briefs, tracing each limitation, part, relationship, and figure statement back to the disclosure.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md (sole technical authority) and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure and adds nothing); input/brief.md was used only for formalities (title status, applicant/inventor "Nimo Rotem", no priority claim, no federal sponsorship), and all sixteen claims, all twenty-five numerals, all four figure briefs, the Brief Description, Summary, Detailed Description, and Abstract were checked and traced item by item. Ledger result: every structural element traces to an exact affirmative passage — connector channel with controllable contactor, connector current sensor, control-pilot interface and local connector identifier ("Each connector has a controllable contactor, a connector current sensor, a control-pilot interface, and a local connector identifier"); branch current sensor upstream of the connector contactors ("A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"); isolated local bus limited to interfaces and contactors ("communicates with the connector interfaces and contactors over an isolated local bus"); network interface, nonvolatile memory holding the signed local authorization token and last accepted branch limit, service input, and local fault indicator all appear verbatim in the disclosure. Every allocation limitation in claims 1 and 11 (stored charging authorization, requested current, minimum sustaining current, energy-deficit value; subtraction of measured non-charging branch load and configurable safety reserve from the branch limit; sustaining-current-first then deficit distribution; pilot send plus connector-sensor verification) matches the second disclosure paragraph word for word in substance. Claims 2 and 12 (re-measure after each opening, open no further contactor) are entailed by "opens connector contactors one at a time in a stored shedding order until measured branch current is below the branch limit"; claims 3 and 13 by the three-condition reclosure sentence; claims 4 and 14 by the welded-contactor/leakage-threshold/inhibit/fault-indicator sentence; claims 6–8 and 15 by the network-outage paragraph; claims 9, 10 and 16 by the service-input paragraph, including "stored only after the sensed channel agrees with the commanded connector". The reduced-pilot-command trigger recited in claims 1 and 11 and at step 210 is supported by the disclosure's staged-reduction relationship ("staged reduction followed by ordered contactor shedding when branch current does not respond") read with "If measured branch current remains above the branch limit after a reduced pilot command for a verification interval". Figure geometry was checked for substantive assertions: the FIG. 2 placement of the connector current sensor downstream of the contactor and between it and the vehicle connector is compelled by the disclosed welded-contactor test ("connector current remains above a leakage threshold after an open command") and the zero-current reclosure condition; the FIG. 1 placement of the branch current sensor upstream of all three drops is compelled by "measures total current upstream of the connector contactors" combined with the subtraction of a "measured non-charging branch load"; the remaining outlines (dashed installation boundary, empty blocks, small square contactor, small circle sensor, rounded-rectangle vehicle) are generic, labelled "shown schematically", carry no proportions, materials, counts or functional-face relationships, and are not verbalized as examples or optional shapes anywhere in the application text. Internal checks: each numeral denotes exactly one part across the ledger, description and briefs; every numeral in the table appears in at least one figure and in the description; FIG. 4 contains exactly six rectangles and two diamonds matching the eight step numerals 202–216 and its two return paths match the described interval loop and post-reclosure re-entry; no section lines exist, so no designation matching applies; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains. The abstract is 146 words, within the 150-word limit. One verified internal inconsistency is reported: two FIG. 1 numeral entries locate leaders on a "square outline" that the body of that brief never introduces (the branch current sensor there is described as a rectangle). No unsupported technical assertion was found in the claims, description or figure briefs.

findings.title: FIG. 1 numeral entries place leaders on a "square outline" that the FIG. 1 body never defines
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, numeral entries for 102 (branch conductor) and 104 (branch current sensor), read against the body sentence describing the branch current sensor
findings.detail: The body of the FIG. 1 brief introduces the branch current sensor as a rectangle, but both numeral entries direct the leaders to a "square outline", a shape that is never introduced in FIG. 1 (a "small empty square outline" is the contactor 122 in FIG. 2). The renderer is given two conflicting shape descriptions for the same element in one brief, and the 102 leader is positioned relative to an undefined feature. This is a self-consistency defect in the brief only; the underlying element (branch current sensor on the branch conductor upstream of the drops) is fully supported by the disclosure ("A branch current sensor measures total current upstream of the connector contactors"), so no invention matter is added or removed by the fix.
findings.evidence: Body: "An empty rectangle stands on this horizontal line in its left portion and represents the branch current sensor, shown schematically. The horizontal line meets the left side of that rectangle and leaves its right side..." Numerals: "- 102 branch conductor: leader ends on the horizontal line, right of the square outline and clear of the vertical drops." and "- 104 branch current sensor: leader ends on the square outline."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the 102 entry to read "102 branch conductor: leader ends on the horizontal line, right of the branch current sensor rectangle and clear of the vertical drops." and change the 104 entry to read "104 branch current sensor: leader ends on the outline of the rectangle that interrupts the horizontal line." Make no other change; the body sentence describing the rectangle stays as drafted.
